Laborer arrested for stabbing friend in QC; jealousy eyed. A 39-year-old construction worker was arrested after allegedly stabbing his 40-year-old friend, a jeepney barker, in Barangay Commonwealth, Quezon City, Wednesday night, Aug. 19, reportedly out of jealousy. Batasan Police Station commander Lt. Col. Gemmer Tubiera said the stabbing occurred at around 8 p.m. on a roadside where the victim was working. Police said the suspect went to the victim’s workplace and asked him to talk before allegedly bringing him to a dark portion of the road, where he stabbed the victim and fled. The two men were reportedly drinking when the incident happened. Investigation showed that days before the stabbing, the suspect allegedly drove the victim out of their shared residence after becoming jealous over a woman they both liked. Tubiera said the suspect became angry after learning that the victim had been texting the woman. The victim suffered a stab wound on his left arm and was taken to a hospital, where he is recovering. The suspect was arrested during a follow-up operation in Fairview, Quezon City, on Aug. 19. Police recovered from him the knife allegedly used in the stabbing, which still had bloodstains. The suspect denied stabbing his friend, claiming that the victim slipped while holding a knife. “I did not stab him. He was holding a knife and accidentally slipped while holding it,” he said. He also denied that jealousy was the motive, claiming that he only intended to confront the victim after accusing him of teaching his child to steal. “It’s not true,” he said when asked about the alleged jealousy. The suspect remains in the custody of the Batasan Police Station and is set to face a complaint for frustrated murder.

Erwin Tulfo: Up to Ombudsman to determine if Guteza committed perjury. Sen. Erwin Tulfo on Thursday, Aug. 20, said he would leave it to the Office of the Ombudsman to determine whether flood control mess witness Orly Guteza should face charges after recanting his earlier testimony on alleged cash deliveries to politicians. Tulfo, who chairs the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee, said the panel welcomed Guteza's decision to retract his previous statements, which he described as false and damaging to several people who were allegedly implicated in his testimony. “Ako’y, nagpapasalamat naman nahimasmasan sila at nagsabi sila ng totoo (I’m thankful that they came to their senses and told the truth),” Tulfo said in a DZBB interview. He said the Ombudsman should determine whether Guteza committed perjury, particularly since the anti-graft body is already handling the broader investigation into alleged irregularities in flood control projects. Tulfo said having the Blue Ribbon Committee conduct its own investigation into Guteza's recantation would only delay the proceedings because any findings would eventually have to be referred to the Ombudsman for prosecution. “It's a waste of time,” Tulfo said, noting that the Senate committee had already turned over documents concerning the flood control controversy to the Ombudsman. Guteza's surprise appearance before a Senate Blue Ribbon Committee hearing on Sept. 25, 2025 drew attention after he claimed that he and several companions personally delivered suitcases containing cash to the residences of Leyte 1st District Rep. Martin Romualdez and then-Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co. Guteza's latest recantation also included allegations that former congressman Mike Defensor and Sen. Rodante Marcoleta had encouraged him to give the false testimony. Tulfo said those allegations further strengthen the case for the Ombudsman to take over the matter, noting that the anti-graft body had previously filed cases against Defensor and Marcoleta. “If there is perjury or being an accomplice or lying by a witness, all the more it should be the Ombudsman that handles it,” Tulfo said. Meanwhile, Tulfo said the Blue Ribbon Committee's membership is nearly complete following the entry of Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano. He said the panel was still awaiting representation for the social justice panel. Tulfo said he would convene the committee to determine its next course of action. He said the panel may focus on investigating allegedly substandard roads and bridges, while leaving the flood control-related cases to the Ombudsman to expedite the prosecution of government officials who may be held responsible. Not surprising For Senator Panfilo "Ping" Lacson, Guteza's recantation doesn't come as a surprise. Lacson was the head of the blue ribbon panel when Guteza made his previous statements. "Since on record naman sa hearing ng Blue Ribbon Committee na coached witness ni Sen Marcoleta si Guteza at naka live pa nga, hindi na surprising na babaliktad siya balang araw (Since it’s already on record during the Blue Ribbon Committee hearing that Guteza was a coached witness of Sen. Marcoleta, and it was even aired live, it’s no longer surprising that he would eventually recant)," he said.

Former Wimby finalist Nick Kyrgios suspended after positive test for cocaine. GENEVA (AP) — Former Wimbledon finalist Nick Kyrgios revealed on Wednesday, Aug. 19, he tested positive for cocaine, and cited the doping case as a wake up call after feeling “helpless and alone” as injuries derailed his career. The 31-year-old Australian with a checkered disciplinary record was provisionally suspended after playing just 10 singles matches on the ATP tour, winning only two, since his peak season of 2022. Then, he reached the final at the grass-court Grand Slam and lost to Novak Djokovic. Kyrgios is now ranked 919th. He tested positive in June for the party drug during a lower-tier grass court event in Spain. “I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine,” he wrote on his Instagram account. “I made a huge mistake and take full responsibility for it.” It is the latest negative headline in the career of a talented though fiery personality, whose highest profile action on court in recent years was a curious “Battle of the Sexes” win over Aryna Sabalenka in Dubai last December. Kyrgios faces a ban of up to four years, though a lighter sanction can be expected. Cocaine is banned as a doping substance during competitions, with lower sanctions applied when used away from events. In a similar case in 2017, British player Dan Evans served a one-year ban imposed by the International Tennis Federation for testing positive for cocaine at the Barcelona Open. Struggling with injuries Kyrgios said he had difficulties coming to terms with being near the end of his career after two years of injuries. “At times I’ve felt helpless and alone. None of that excuses what I did,” he said. He added the injuries "have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally. My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do.” Kyrgios has a 1-3 record in singles this year and got a wild card to play doubles at Wimbledon last month. He lost in the first round with partner Alexander Bublik. The International Tennis Integrity Agency will prosecute the case and said the player's sample was taken on June 22 and the positive test was confirmed on July 17, after Kyrgios played at Wimbledon. A mandatory provisional suspension was applied on Aug. 4 and has not been appealed by Kyrgios, the ITIA added. Kyrgios sees a way back “However, the good news is that this has given me a wake up call,” Kyrgios wrote, signaling his career is not over. “For the next 28 days I'll be stepping away from social media and public life while I focus on getting myself right.” Career decline since 2022 The most recent of Kyrgios' seven career singles titles was won in his first tournament after the Wimbledon final. He beat Yoshihito Nishioka in the final of the hard-court event in Washington, D.C., in August 2022. Weeks later he reached the U.S. Open quarterfinals, losing to Karen Khachanov. After a knee injury in Tokyo in October 2022, Kyrgios played just once in the next two years, citing a wrist injury to miss Wimbledon in 2023. Kyrgios had a meager 1-4 record in the 2025 season, losing a first-round match in the Australian Open then skipping the next three Grand Slams.

Finally! AFP to review policies, procedures on recruitment, conferment of awards to reservists. The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) finally noticed, and is now doing something about the policies and procedures governing its Reserve Force following a social media backlash over a photo of a reservist who has more medals than the highest military official in the country. In a statement, the AFP said it is also conducting an investigation to establish the facts and determine whether any irregularities or violations of existing policies and regulations have occurred. “The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) is reviewing its policies and procedures on the recruitment, promotion, and conferment of awards to personnel of the Reserve Force,” the statement read. “An investigation through the Philippine Air Force is likewise being undertaken to establish the facts and determine whether any irregularities or violations of existing policies and regulations have occurred,” it added. Last week, social media was abuzz on how a reservist has more medals than the incumbent AFP Chief of Staff, in a photo posted after a confirmation before the Commission on Appointments— Gen. Antonio Nafarrete as AFP chief of staff, and a former solon as Brigadier General of the military’s Reserve Force. The viral photo sparked complaints and concerns not only on social media but also on chat groups of retired and active uniformed personnel over the recruitment and promotion in the military’ reserve force. Promotion is hard especially in the military and some soldiers called out the AFP over the recruitment and promotions of popular and influential personalities who did not even fire a single shot against an enemy, and were even incapable of doing 10 push-ups. For some retired and active soldiers, every promotion and award must be earned in order to avoid various misconceptions in the entire process. And this is what the AFP wants to ensure in the conduct of review into the incident, “The AFP remains committed to upholding the integrity, meritocracy, and credibility of its processes. Any verified irregularities shall be addressed in accordance with existing rules and regulations.” Despite the ongoing review, the AFP said “it recognizes the valuable contributions of its reservists and will continue to ensure that the standards governing the Reserve Force are properly observed.”

BIR files ₱2-billion tax case against offshore gaming operator Hongsheng. The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) filed a ₱2.23 billion tax evasion case against offshore online gaming operator Hongsheng Gaming Technology Inc. after its investigation uncovered underreporting of revenues and unremitted taxes. In a statement, BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza said the tax authority lodged the criminal complaint with the Department of Justice (DOJ) on Aug. 6, targeting the company’s operations covering taxable years 2021 through 2023. According to the BIR, investigation records showed Hongsheng substantially underdeclared its taxable income, misstated value-added tax liabilities across multiple quarters, and failed to withhold and remit final withholding tax due on foreign employees. Investigators cited significant discrepancies between Hongsheng’s declared earnings and cross-referenced official records from other government institutions. The total tax deficiency consists of ₱2.2 billion spread across unpaid corporate income tax, value-added tax, and employee withholding taxes. “Honest taxpayers deserve a level playing field,” Mendoza said. “No business should be able to operate in the Philippines, earn income here, and evade the taxes required by law. The BIR will pursue these cases wherever the evidence leads us.” The legal action forms part of the tax agency’s broader Run After Tax Evaders initiative, an ongoing enforcement program aimed at cracking down on illicit corporate schemes that weaken the national tax base and disadvantage compliant entities.

Take care of cops deployed for disaster response, PNP commanders told. Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr., chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP), ordered all police commanders to ensure strong support systems to their men who are deployed for disaster response duty amid the effects of heavy rains in the past days. Part of that support system, he said, are protection and equipment for the prevailing weather conditions, especially in flooded areas where policemen were deployed to conduct rescue, relief, and public assistance operations. “While our mandate is to serve and protect all our kababayan in times of serious flooding and other calamities, we also have the obligation to look after the welfare of all our personnel not only for better response but also to ensure their safety,” said Nartatez. “Each and every PNP personnel deployed for disaster response has family too and as commanders, we have to make sure that they are taken care of in order for them to go home safely,” he added. More than 600 police officers had been deployed to assist residents affected by the rains and flooding. Policemen have also continued assisting stranded commuters through free rides in areas affected by inundation. Nartatez also ordered assistance for personnel whose families were affected by the massive flooding, “We will also provide psychosocial support for our men, especially those whose families have also been affected by the massive floods brought by torrential rains.” He said the support is intended to help police personnel who continue reporting for duty while dealing with the impact of the disaster on their own families.

SM Expands ‘Green Recycling Machine’ network to boost nationwide recycling. What if your used plastic bottle could become part of something much bigger? Through the right machine, it can! SM Cares, through the SM Green Movement, has partnered with recycling technology company Sparklo to deploy SM Green Recycling Machines to 30 SM Supermalls across the country. Through the nationwide deployment across SM’s network of most-loved malls, responsible waste disposal becomes easier, more engaging, and more rewarding for mallgoers. The reverse vending machines empower customers to deposit eligible plastic bottles in exchange for rewards. The partnership turns simple mall, customer visits into pathways to help support the SM Green Movement through responsible waste management and segregation to divert waste away from landfills and maximize resources through recycling. SM Green Recycling Machines are now available in key locations across Metro Manila, Batangas, Laguna, Cavite, Bulacan, Pampanga, Baguio, Pangasinan, La Union, Rizal, and Cebu. Each plastic bottle placed in the machines represents more than properly managed waste. It is a small but meaningful choice that helps keep recyclable materials in circulation, supports responsible consumption, and brings communities closer to an SM Waste-Free Future. The partnership forms part of the SM Cares Environmental Sustainability Program under its Waste Management Pillar. It complements SM’s existing circular economy and waste management efforts, including the Trash to Cash Program and the Plastic Waste Collection Program. Through initiatives like these, SM Cares seeks to make sustainable living easier to understand and practice. Rather than asking people to make sweeping changes all at once, the SM Green Recycling Machines show how everyday actions—repeated by families, students, young people, and communities—can collectively create lasting environmental impact. With Sparklo’s technology and the reach of SM Supermalls, recycling becomes more than a responsibility. It becomes a convenient and rewarding habit that Filipinos can carry into their daily lives—one plastic bottle and one better choice at a time.

2 dead, 4 hurt in Ilocos Sur SUV-truck collision. BANTAY, Ilocos Sur — Two people were killed and four others were injured after a sports utility vehicle (SUV) collided head‑on with a truck along the national highway in Barangay Banaoang here before dawn Wednesday, Aug. 19. Police identified the fatalities as the 22‑year‑old driver of the SUV and one of its passengers, also 22. Both victims were residents of Mangaldan, Pangasinan. The truck was driven by a 48‑year‑old man from Anda, Pangasinan, who sustained minor injuries in the crash. According to Police Lt. Ronie Corpuz of the Bantay Municipal Police Station, the truck was traveling northbound when the SUV allegedly crossed into its lane, resulting in the head‑on collision. The impact caused severe injuries to the SUV driver and passenger, resulting in their deaths. Four other passengers of the SUV were also injured and rushed to the nearest hospital. An earlier police account said the SUV was carrying six people and was believed to have come from Laoag, Ilocos Norte. Both vehicles were heavily damaged, with the SUV almost unrecognizable after the crash. Police said the investigation remains ongoing. Authorities are also awaiting the results of medico‑legal examinations to determine whether alcohol or other factors were involved. The Bantay police urged motorists to exercise caution and drive responsibly, stressing that road safety is a shared responsibility.

Woman shot dead in Antipolo, found wearing dog tag. Authorities are hunting four suspects who allegedly gunned down a woman found wearing a dog tag in Antipolo City late Tuesday, Aug. 18. The Antipolo Component City Police Station said the incident occurred around 11:55 p.m. beside Seminario Church in Barangay Inarawan. Initial investigation showed the victim, still unidentified, was standing near the church on a dark, rainy night when four men aboard two motorcycles approached her. For no apparent reason, police said, the suspects opened fire with firearms of undetermined caliber before fleeing in an unknown direction. The victim was rushed to Mambugan Hospital but was declared dead on arrival. Authorities said she was found wearing a dog tag inscribed with the name “Aiza.” “The victim’s remains are subject to autopsy examination by the appropriate forensic authorities to determine the exact cause and manner of death and to assist in the ongoing investigation,” Antipolo police said in a statement. Investigators are working to establish the motive, identify the victim, and track down the suspects.

DSWD starts trauma support for students after Zamboanga school shooting. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) has started providing psychological first aid (PFA) to students affected by the shooting incident at the Ateneo de Zamboanga University (ADZU). Eight students aged 11 to 14 received PFA from DSWD mental health professionals on Aug. 19, a day after the shooting incident involving a minor. “The intervention provided by the DSWD to the students was done in a safe and supportive space where they could process their emotions, express their concerns, and learn healthy coping strategies as they deal with the psychological impact of the traumatic experience,” DSWD Assistant Secretary and spokesperson Irene Dumlao said on Thursday, Aug. 20. DSWD-Field Office 9 in Zamboanga Peninsula is set to provide PFA to ADZU teachers and staff on Thursday as the agency expands its response beyond the students directly affected by the incident. The department also plans to provide aftercare services and other interventions, including Enhanced Trauma-Informed Care, medical assistance and Parent Effectiveness Sessions (PES), depending on the needs of those affected. Dumlao said DSWD Secretary Rex Gatchalian assured school administrators that the agency would continue supporting the school community during a meeting following the incident. “As the Secretary instructed, next week the Department scheduled a Trauma Psychosocial Support Training for frontline responders and duty-bearers who responded in the Zamboanga school shooting incident,” Dumlao said. “Our aim is to teach responders with appropriate knowledge and skills to ensure that they are equipped to provide psychosocial support and are sensitive to the needs of trauma survivors,” she added. The multidisciplinary training is intended to equip responders and other stakeholders with skills to provide appropriate psychosocial support and aftercare to trauma survivors.

‘Talk to your child’: Erwin Tulfo urges parents amid series of school shooting incidents. Please talk to your children, talk to your child. Senator Erwin Tulfo on Thursday, August 20 made the call to parents as he lamented the death of two more students in a shooting case at the Ateneo de Zamboanga University, while saying he believes that the incident “should be a lesson for everybody.” “What happened po, not only in Zamboanga but also in Tacloban, Leyte, two shooting incidents, I think, hindi lang po the school failed, everybody failed. The school, the family, the parents failed. Relatives of guardians of those children failed,” Tulfo said during the Senate Committee on Women and Children’s hearing on the issue. “…(The)parents po, because we're so busy, because we have work, we're so engrossed with many things in life, nagpapabayaan na po natin mga anak natin (we are neglecting our children). We don't talk to them. We don't communicate with our children. Siguro po, once in a while, we have to say, “kumusta anak (how are you, child)?” di ba. Over dinner, over lunch, or during the weekend, just ask our child,” Tulfo pointed out. “This should be a lesson for everybody, for every parent attending here and listening to this hearing. Please, please talk to your children, talk to your child. Kung nag-iisa po yan (If he’s alone), you think he's okay, or she's okay, para malaman muna niyo (so you would know) what's going on inside his or her mind,” he said. “Malay mo hindi po siya bayolente pero (Maybe he’s not violent but) deep down inside she wants to heal, or wants to end his or her life. There's so many instances…they're so fragile. But it's because napapabayaan po natin (we neglet them). We don't communicate with them. Because we're so busy. The dad is busy with work. The mom is busy with work or business. Leaving the child to the yaya, to the katulong, or to somebody, to the grandma,” he further noted. “We have to start acting now before it's too late. We have to start dealing with it. talking to them, kahit once a week lang. ‘How's school, anak?’ I do that to my child. I talk to them. ‘How are you? How's school? Everything okay?’,” he stressed. At the same time, Tulfo said schools should take threats seriously, citing reports that there were already warnings of a possible shooting had already been circulating prior to the incident. He also raised concerns over inequality over school security protocols, saying students who arrive in school by tricycle, pedicab or on foot are subjected to stricter screening, while students who are arriving by car would be allowed to enter the premises with just a salute to the security officer. Tulfo said this could have been the reason the shooter was able to the bring the firearms inside the school. Nevertheless, he said it is imperative that parents do not assume that their children are doing well even if they have good academic standing. “Please, please, before it's too late, talk to your children, talk to your son, all of them. Kung may isang malungkutin (If one is always sad), talk to the child. Kung may isang masiglahin (if one is so energetic) still, talk to the child. because we'll never know. Because that might be the last day, the last day that he or she leaves for school, that's the last day that we see him or her alive,” he appealed.

'No forensic evidence': Ex-IBP president slams Ombudsman's probe on Romualdez. A former national president of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) has criticized the quality--of lack thereof--of the Ombudsman's investigation on Leyte 1st district Rep. Martin Romualdez when it comes to the flood control projects mess. Lawyer Ade Fajardo, Romualdez's legal counsel, said the investigation had been ongoing for months now. He noted that the Ombudsman had broad authority to summon witnesses and obtain records. “Ang kapansin-pansin lang dito is this investigation has been going on for several months. Lumalabas, wala man lang forensic evidence or object or documentary evidence linking the former Speaker,” he said in a press conference Thursday, Aug. 20. (The investigation has been going on for several months. It turns out, there is no forensic evidence or object or documentary evidence linking the former Speaker.) Fajardo slammed what he described as reliance on oral accounts that had changed over time. "Alam naman natin, ito iyong pinaka-unreliable (We know is the most unreliable). That's why we have laws on perjury, libel, et cetera, kasi (because) these things are easily manufactured,” he said. Four of the original 18 “Maleta Boys”--accusers of Romualdez when it comes to alleged flood control payoffs--earlier recanted. Guteza, who separately testified before the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee in September 2025 that he delivered suitcases ("maleta") containing cash to Romualdez, also withdrew his allegation in a new affidavit reported on Aug. 19. Other witnesses have stood by their earlier statements. One alleged that millions of pesos had been offered to induce recantations, while lawyer Levi Baligod submitted a flash drive that he said was relevant to the reversals. Romualdez's camp denied influencing or paying any witness. 'Non-case' The recantations have led Fajardo to call the Ombudsman's supposed case a "non-case". "It should be dismissed kasi wala nang ebidensya maliban sa kuwento, at ang kuwento ay iba-iba; ang kuwento ay nababaliktad.” (It should be dismissed because there is no evidence other than stories, and the stories are inconsistent; the stories are being retracted.) The ex-speaker's lawyer added that individuals had been included or removed from the accounts as the political climate changed. Fajardo also cited the cyberlibel and perjury cases filed against Baligod and members of the witness group. He said government agencies, including the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and Department of Justice (DOJ), had pursued cyberlibel and perjury cases against members of the group. The perjury complaints concern allegedly false statements made by the witnesses in separate settings. They do not replace the Ombudsman's obligation to evaluate the alleged cash-delivery scheme on its own evidence, just as the recantations do not automatically erase the earlier accounts. Fajardo said Romualdez had answered the accusations and would submit the latest affidavits for consideration.

Hong Kong conglomerate seeks $1.5 billion in damages from Panama for takeover of canal ports. HONG KONG (AP) — Hong Kong conglomerate CK Hutchison said Thursday it was seeking more than $1.5 billion in damages from Panama after the country seized two canal ports caught in the crosshairs of U.S.-China tensions. CK Hutchison said in the statement that it had begun new arbitration proceedings against Panama and alleged that the Central American country had breached an investment protection treaty through “sovereign acts that targeted a decades-old ports concession” in a “state attack campaign” on the company’s assets in the Central American country. Panama’s government in February seized the Balboa and Cristobal ports, located on each end of the Panama Canal, after its Supreme Court that a concession held by CK Hutchison’s subsidiary to run the two ports was unconstitutional. The two ports at each end of the Panama Canal became part of U.S.-China tensions since Donald Trump’s return to the White House last year after he alleged China of “running” the canal. The Panama Canal is managed and owned by Panama. But CK Hutchison’s subsidiary Panama Ports Company had run the two ports on the canal from 1997 and had renewed its concession for 25 years in 2021. Beijing and Hong Kong had hit back at Panama over its takeover of the ports. CK Hutchison, controlled by the family of Hong Kong’s richest man Li Ka-shing, last year announced an initial $23 billion deal to sell its global ports business, including the two Panama ports, to a consortium involving U.S. investment firm BlackRock. But the deal had made little progress under geopolitical tensions and legal challenges among China, the U.S. and Panama. In March, Panama Ports Company had separately sought at least $2 billion in compensation from Panama over its takeover of the ports which it said was unlawful under international arbitration proceedings. CK Hutchison said the actions were making progress. CK Hutchison added that Thursday's new proceedings were focused on its treaty rights, which were distinct from Panama Ports Company’s contract rights in the earlier arbitration proceedings. In April, the subsidiary also launched arbitration proceedings against Danish shipping and logistics group Maersk after it took over some of its port operations in Panama. Maersk said at the time that it did not believe it was liable for the claims.

Prince Harry and Meghan are returning to the UK with their children. LONDON (AP) — Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, have decided to return to the United Kingdom for an extended stay starting this fall, but they won’t resume their roles as working members of the royal family, The Associated Press learned Wednesday. The couple's children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, have already enrolled at British schools and will start classes in September, according to a person close to the Sussexes who was not authorized to speak publicly. The family plans to live at a private, non-royal residence outside of London, but plans to maintain their home in Montecito, California, and their vacation property in Portugal. The Daily Telegraph first reported the story. When asked to discuss the reports by the AP at a roundtable event with U.S. veterans in Washington Wednesday night, Harry replied, "Nothing to say.” Harry and Meghan gave up their royal duties and moved to California more than six years ago to earn their living through lucrative contracts with Netflix and Spotify. Although relations with the rest of the royal family have soured since then, Harry has recently expressed an interest in reconciliation so he could spend more time with his father, King Charles III, who is being treated for an undisclosed form of cancer. Charles was informed of the couple's plans on Sunday. Harry and Meghan visited the U.K. last month. Buckingham Palace has a policy of not commenting on speculation about non-working members of the royal family. A representative for Harry and Meghan declined to comment. According to a source close to the Sussexes, Meghan will continue heading her As Ever company from the U.K., while Harry can spend more time working with his U.K.-based charities. Harry and Meghan have had a stormy relationship with the royal family ever since they decamped to a mansion in the exclusive Southern California enclave of Montecito. In a series of interviews and Harry's memoir “Spare,” the couple said they left Britain to escape the restrictions of royal life and criticized palace officials for being insensitive to Meghan's mental health while alleging that at least one member of the royal family had expressed racist views when she was pregnant with their first child. Meghan describes herself as biracial. Those tensions were exacerbated by Harry's long-running legal battle with Britain's tabloid newspapers, which he alleges illegally hacked his phones and invaded his privacy when he was younger. The prince has lost a series of lawsuits against the media, including one against the publisher of the Daily Mail, which concluded last month. The latest trial has left Harry facing a potential bill for millions of pounds after the court ruled he and other plaintiffs in the case were liable for the publisher's legal fees. Associated Newspapers has filed documents showing that its legal costs amounted to 34.5 million pounds ($47 million). Harry has also been embroiled in a legal wrangle with the British government after a government committee refused to authorize police protection for the prince and his family when they are in the U.K. The prince says he and his family need armed police protection because they are at risk simply because they are members of the royal family, regardless of whether they are working royals. After losing a court battle over the security issue last year, Harry said he hoped to rebuild relations with his family. “I would love reconciliation with my family. There’s no point in continuing to fight anymore,” Harry told the BBC. “I don’t know how much longer my father has.” Last month, Harry returned to the U.K. for a series of charity engagements. Meghan and the children joined Harry for part of the visit and they spent time with the king at his Highgrove estate in western England. It was the first time Archie and Lilibet had seen their grandfather since the late Queen Elizabeth II's platinum jubilee in 2022. While Harry has recently met with his father, there are no signs of a warming of relations with his brother, Prince William, the heir to the throne. Peter Hunt, a former BBC royal correspondent, said the surprise announcement would make William “apoplectic.” “In the short term, Harry will be able to deepen his rapprochement with his father," Hunt told Britain's Press Association. “And his presence back home will make it harder for his brother to duck a reconciliation."

Pumping stations won't solve flood woes alone — Marcos. While the government is eyeing the completion of upgrades and the construction of 13 pumping stations in Metro Manila, President Marcos admitted that these measures alone will not solve the perennial flooding problem in the metropolis. In an interview during his inspection of the Tripa de Gallina Pumping Station in Pasay City on Thursday, Aug. 20, Marcos said improper waste disposal will continue to affect the efficiency of pumping stations if it will not be addressed. "Okay naman, malakas naman ang mga bomba natin, umaandar naman sila lahat. Pero ang nagiging problema pa rin ay yung pagpasok ng basura (Everything is fine, and our pumps are strong. They are all operating. But the problem remains the entry of garbage into the pumping stations)," Marcos said. "Kaya't naghahanap tayo ng mga iba’t ibang pamamaraan upang magamit yung basura at iyan ginagawang compost, ginagawang paso na organic, tapos yung iba kailangan talaga itapon sa landfill (That’s why we are looking for different ways to make use of the waste—turning it into compost, making organic plant pots, while some of it really needs to be disposed of in landfills)," Marcos added. The President stressed the need to address the problem on waste management as it will lead to the decline of the pumping stations' functions. "Kaya't yun ang kailangan natin ayusin talaga. Kahit na maganda ang ating pumping station, kahit malakas ang ating mga bomba, kapag nandyan pa rin, pumapasok pa rin ang basura, syempre ang efficiency niyan bababa, hindi na masyado maganda ang takbo. Kaya 'yan ang kailangan natin ayusin ngayon (“That’s what we really need to address. Even if our pumping stations are in good condition and our pumps are powerful, if garbage continues to enter the system, their efficiency will inevitably decline, and they will not operate as effectively. That’s what we need to address now)," Marcos said. New pumping stations Thirteen pumping stations around Metro Manila are eyed for completion by the end of this year or early next year, Marcos said. "We are installing additional pumping stations and those pumping stations are in and around Manila. I think altogether we will have 13 additional pumping stations which we should have in place by the end of this year or the beginning of next year. Most of them should be in place already," Marcos said. According to Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) Don Artes, of the 13 pumping stations, four of them are newly-built while the rest had undergone upgrade. Marcos, however, stressed that the construction and upgrade of new pumping stations "does not solve our problem with garbage." "So that is why we are here trying to find ways to dispose of the garbage in an environmentally friendly way. That's why they are creating compost. None of the organic waste goes to waste as it were. Lahat ng organic waste nagagamit (All organic waste will be be used)," Marcos said. The Chief Executive said all inorganic waste being thrown into the system is "where we are encountering problems." "Ang biro nga nila is that kung kukunin mo lahat ng lumalabas na basura, pwede kang magbuo ng bahay dahil meron mga kitchen sink, may mattress tayo nakita, may kung ano-ano yung kinatapon (As they often joke, if you collected all the garbage that comes out, you could build a house because we have found kitchen sinks, mattresses, and all sorts of things that people have thrown away)," Marcos said. "Kaya kailangan talagang, kailangan natin tugunan yung problema sa basura (This is why we really need to address the waste problem)," he added. According to the President, waste-to-energy efforts should be put into action by next year, "as long as the financing is available."

11 families evacuated amid landslide threat in Taguig. The Taguig City government ordered the forced evacuation of 11 families along C5 Road on Wednesday, Aug. 19, due to the threat of a landslide and other hazards. Barangay Western Bicutan said the evacuation and road closure were carried out to ensure residents’ safety. The City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office’s Search and Rescue Team, the Public Order and Safety Office, and the Taguig police conducted an ocular assessment in high risk areas of the barangay. The city government also removed a wall that had tilted and collapsed onto C5 Road. The City Social Welfare and Development Office and Barangay Western Bicutan coordinated to ensure the orderly evacuation of affected families. Continuous rains brought by the southwest monsoon have flooded areas across Metro Manila, including Taguig.

UST student councils slam delayed class suspension amid flooding. The Central Student Council and Local Student Councils of the University of Santo Tomas (UST) have condemned what they described as the delayed suspension of classes and response to flooding during severe weather on August 17, saying the decision left thousands of students facing dangerous travel conditions in Manila. In a statement, the student councils criticized both the Manila City Government and the UST administration over the timing of the suspension, saying students had already traveled to or arrived at their campuses by the time classes were called off. They said students were forced to navigate flooded roads, severe traffic, and limited transportation as weather conditions deteriorated across Metro Manila. The councils also questioned the decision to shift to online instruction after the suspension, saying students who had already been placed in unsafe conditions were still expected to attend classes and comply with academic requirements through UST’s Enriched Virtual Mode. “No student should ever be forced to choose between pursuing education and protecting their safety,” the councils said. The student leaders said the worsening weather and flooding were not entirely unforeseen, citing weather monitoring, flood advisories, and previous experiences with similar conditions as sufficient warning of the deteriorating situation. They said thousands of Thomasians were stranded not only on the UST Manila campus but also in various parts of Manila, with some students reportedly forced to stay overnight because of flooded streets and blocked roads. Students from outside Metro Manila likewise faced difficulties traveling home, according to the statement. The councils acknowledged the efforts of students and university offices that assisted during the flooding but said the situation raised questions about the timeliness of the response and the availability of immediate support for those affected. They called on the Manila City Government to strengthen its responsibility toward students, faculty, and workers who study, work, and travel within the city. The student councils also urged the UST administration to adopt more preventive measures, respond more quickly to weather-related concerns, and consider calls for early class suspensions during natural disasters and other emergencies. They likewise called on the national government and lawmakers to address what they described as persistent problems in flood control and disaster preparedness, linking the August 17 flooding to broader concerns over governance and alleged corruption. The councils emphasized that safety decisions should be made before dangerous conditions become widespread. “Students should not have to wait until the streets are flooded before their safety is considered,” they said, adding that waiting for danger to arrive does not constitute preparedness. The Manila City Government and UST administration have yet to issue a response to the student councils’ statement.

Faith healer, 84, slain in Negros home. BACOLOD CITY – An 84‑year‑old faith healer was stabbed to death while sleeping beside his wife inside their house in Don Hermino Village, Barangay 1, E.B. Magalona, Negros Occidental, on Wednesday, Aug. 19. Police identified the victim as Bay, also a pedicab driver. Police Master Sgt. Henry Mangana III said two unidentified men wearing bonnets entered the couple’s home and attacked Bay with a knife while he and his 67‑year‑old wife were asleep. The victim sustained multiple stab wounds and was declared dead at a hospital. His wife suffered minor injuries to her hand when she tried to intervene. Investigators are looking into whether the attack was connected to Bay’s work as a faith healer or to personal grudges. Mangana noted the victim had no police record. Authorities said the assailants targeted only Bay. Police have yet to identify the perpetrators, with limited information available as the victim’s wife, the lone witness, is mourning her husband’s death.

SM Prime taps vast land bank to ride e-commerce logistics boom. SM Prime Holdings Inc. (SM Prime), through its industrial leasing arm SM Warehouses, is looking to expand its logistics facilities nationwide—banking on the group’s immense land bank to serve the growing e-commerce sector. “Right now, we want to maximize SM Prime’s land bank and that it really is nationwide. If there are opportunities… we will definitely take a look at it,” said SM Prime Vice President and Head of Commercial Property Group Alexis Ortiga in a recent media briefing. He explained, “we’re really looking at third-party logistics providers, e-commerce platforms, and even regional warehousing as our tenant partners,” adding, “while we currently don’t have plans to establish industrial parks, we do, and we can do, build-to-suit facilities that could accommodate manufacturing operations.” SM Warehouses sees demand for logistics facilities and warehouses increasing due to the growing number of new generation consumers who want fast deliveries for the products they buy online. “Given the current young demographics of the Philippines consisting of Gen Zs [and] millennials, we see e-commerce continuing, which, in turn, will support demand for industrial and logistics space,” said Ortiga. These include fulfillment centers, last-mile in-city distribution hubs, and even specialized storage facilities. Ortiga noted that this growing business “requires distribution centers and last-mile hubs that are closer to cities where most of the orders come from. These last-mile hubs actually complement the bigger regional warehousing facilities that would store more inventory but are a little bit farther from the city itself.” SM Warehouses has just expanded its logistics space for Shopee partners SPX Express (SPX) and Scommerce Philippines Inc. (Scommerce) with the turnover of a new 40,000-square-meter (sqm) facility in Pasig City. “Our strengthening relationship with SPX and Scommerce reflects our commitment to supporting businesses and local MSMEs [micro, small, and medium enterprises] with well-located, adaptable spaces that improve efficiency and enable long-term growth,” said Ortiga. A leading logistics and delivery services provider to businesses across Southeast Asia, Taiwan, and Brazil, SPX previously signed a multi-year lease for approximately 86,000 sqm at the 130,000-sqm Silangan warehouse complex of SM Prime in Laguna province. Scommerce provides warehousing and fulfillment solutions to sellers and businesses operating on Shopee ’s platform. Together, the Pasig and Laguna facilities of SM Prime provide more than 126,000 sqm of logistics space to Shopee’s logistics partners. “As e-commerce evolves, our logistics infrastructure must grow with it. Our facility in Silangan, Laguna established a strong operational base,” said Martin Yu, head of SPX. Yu added, “The new mega first-mile hub in Pasig brings us closer to Metro Manila customers, allowing us to increase processing speed and reduce delivery times. SM Warehouses provides the scale and operating standards we need to serve our sellers and buyers reliably.” The two facilities serve complementary roles within SPX’s logistics network. The Pasig facility will operate as an urban distribution hub, bringing inventory closer to customers across Metro Manila. Designed for high-volume operations, it is expected to increase processing capacity and shorten last-mile delivery times. The larger Silangan facility provides space for regional fulfillment and sorting operations, connecting southern Luzon to SPX’s nationwide distribution network. Large regional facilities provide the scale required for sorting and fulfillment, while urban hubs reduce the distance between products and their final destinations. SM Warehouses provides large-scale logistics and distribution spaces across the Philippines. It offers ready-to-move-in buildings, greenfield spaces, and custom build-to-suit facilities, ranging from 5,000 sqm to over 120,000 sqm.

Man drowns in Sariaya River during heavy rain. SARIAYA, Quezon — A 47‑year‑old man died after being swept away by a strong current while crossing the river in Barangay Sampaloc 2 on Tuesday afternoon. The victim was identified as Armando Albitos, a resident of Purok 7, Barangay Sampaloc Bogon. According to the Sariaya Municipal Police Station, Albitos left his home around 4 p.m. on Thursday, August 18, to check on his cattle on the other side of the river. He failed to return home and was later found in the river within Barangay Sampaloc 2. Investigators believe he was carried off by the current while crossing. His body was recovered at around 8:30 a.m. on Friday, August 19, by a search and rescue team from the Sariaya Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, the Philippine National Police, and residents who joined the search.

Carnapped van recovered after P500K mortgage deal. A van reported as carnapped in Quezon City was recovered in Cavite after police learned that it had allegedly been mortgaged for P500,000. The registered owner reported the 2023 Nissan Urvan Premium to the Quezon City Police District (QCPD) District Anti-Carnapping Unit (DACU) on Aug. 12, saying it had allegedly been taken in May 2024 along Commonwealth Avenue in Barangay Holy Spirit, Quezon City, by alias “Rodolfo.” A carnapping complaint was subsequently filed against the suspect before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office. Acting on the report, DACU personnel conducted verification operations to locate the vehicle. On Aug. 15, police received information that the van was allegedly at Diamond Village in Salawag, Dasmariñas, Cavite. DACU personnel immediately went to the area and confirmed that the vehicle was the subject of the report. The team approached the woman who was in possession of the van, identified themselves, and informed her of its reported status. She told police that “Rodolfo” had allegedly mortgaged the vehicle to her for P500,000. After being informed of the circumstances, the woman voluntarily turned over the van to the police and was brought to the DACU office for further investigation.

IG Official? Magui Ford and Robbie Jaworski share sweet Hong Kong escapade. Recto urges US firms to create jobs, develop Filipino talent. Executive Secretary Ralph Recto urged American companies to expand their investments in the Philippines while creating jobs, developing Filipino talent, and contributing to shared prosperity between the two countries. Speaking to American business leaders at the Welcome Reception for the 2026 Philippines Business Mission on Tuesday, Aug. 18, Recto said the Philippines wanted to turn its decades-old alliance with the United States into a stronger economic partnership. “That is the partnership we want—not just one business mission, but generations of investment, innovation, jobs, and shared prosperity between the Philippines and the United States,” Recto said. He urged members of the US-ASEAN Business Council (USABC) to “Stay in the Philippines. Expand in the Philippines. And build your future in the Philippines.” Recto highlighted the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC), which will link Subic, Clark, Manila, and Batangas as a hub for logistics, manufacturing, connectivity, and innovation, and is expected to generate up to one million jobs. “This is how we can turn an eight-decade alliance into an economic corridor for the next generation,” he said. The Executive Secretary also encouraged US companies to invest in electronics and semiconductors, particularly in advanced packaging, integrated circuit design, research and development, supply-chain resilience, front-end semiconductor capabilities, and critical minerals processing. Recto said the Philippines wanted to move beyond extracting and exporting critical minerals by developing domestic capacity in processing, manufacturing, and innovation. “We want more factories rising here, critical minerals processed—not just extracted and exported. More electronics proudly made in the Philippines. And more Filipino engineers, technicians, and researchers given the chance to thrive,” he said. According to Recto, the Pax Silica partnership could enable American companies to bring technology, capital, research, and training to the Philippines, while also urging them to develop operations that create opportunities for Filipino workers and researchers. “We do not want American companies to simply buy from the Philippines. We want you to bring your technology here. Bring your capital and research here. Train Filipino talent here. And build your next breakthrough here,” he said. Recto said investor confidence would depend on the country's workforce, costs, regulatory environment, infrastructure, and government efficiency, adding that the administration was pursuing reforms to make investments easier, faster, and more predictable. “Your confidence cannot be demanded. It must be earned. And that is exactly what we intend to do,” he said. Among the measures he cited were the CREATE MORE Act, Green Lanes for strategic investments, and the Energy Virtual One-Stop Shop, as well as the opening of additional sectors to foreign participation, including renewable energy and public services such as telecommunications, toll roads, airports, and shipping. Recto also urged US business leaders to identify regulatory and infrastructure problems affecting their operations, including lengthy permitting processes, regulatory uncertainty, and infrastructure gaps, saying the government was prepared to address them. “When government becomes the obstacle to growth, government must change—not the ambition, not the investments, and certainly not the opportunity,” he said. The Philippines Business Mission is an annual engagement organized by the USABC to strengthen US-Philippines economic and business relations, with the council representing more than 180 global corporations operating in ASEAN and other markets.

DND, PAOCC hit back at Chinese Embassy in Manila over 'selective law enforcement' claim. The Department of National Defense (DND) hit back at the Chinese Embassy in Manila for allegedly defending those behind the operation of a steel manufacturing company raided over alleged substandard products and hazardous workplace. In a statement, the DND said the statement issued by the Chinese Embassy in Manila that comes with allegations against those that conducted the raid only showed that the latter is now serving as the public relations firm of those involved. “From their public statements in the past days it is obvious that they are covering up for these people. The public is aware of their role which is now obvious,” the statement read. The DND statement was in response to the statement issued by the Chinese Embassy in Manila which insinuated selective implementation of the law in the raid of the Sanjia Steel Corporation in Misamis Oriental. “If Sanjia Steel Corp. allegedly violated environmental or other laws, why were the workers arrested instead of those in charge? Why were only the workers, and Chinese workers in particular arrested, while more than 300 Filipino workers were released on the spot? After all, Chinese and Filipino employees worked side by side every day,” the China Embassy statement posted on social media read. “How can you determine, before any trial or investigation has taken place, that the Filipino workers had done nothing wrong while the 70 Chinese workers were the ones at fault? Is nationality being used as the basis for distinguishing between people and determining guilt? Are Filipinos presumed innocent while Chinese are presumed guilty? Isn’t that precisely selective and targeted law enforcement?,” it added. The DND said such statements of an embassy in the country defending alleged wrongdoings should be condemned. The DND’s statement was backed by the Presidential Anti-Organized Crime Commission (PAOCC) which is one of the agencies at the forefront of conducting operations against steel companies with substandard products and hazardous workplaces. In a separate statement, PAOCC said what the Chinese Embassy in Manila did in posting a statement against legitimate law enforcement clearly disregards diplomatic decorum and the sovereign laws of the Philippines. “As diplomatic representatives hosted by our nation, lecturing host authorities on lawful domestic operations is inappropriate. We challenge the Embassy to allow the same open public dialogue on Chinese social media platforms so that the Chinese people can be informed of the full, transparent facts,” the PAOCC statement read. PAOCC explained that the operation against Sanjia Steel operation was an inter-agency law-enforcement operation and not an action against any nationality. It said the participation of the Armed Forces of the Philippines in the operation is limited to providing security and logistical support and should not be misconstrued as a military operation against Chinese workers. “Arrest or investigation does not mean guilt, and no person, Filipino or foreign, is presumed guilty simply because of citizenship. Any determination on charges, detention, or release remains subject to the proper legal process,” PAOCC said. “It is therefore inaccurate to characterize the operation as selective enforcement against Chinese nationals. For PAOCC and its partner agencies, this is purely a matter of law enforcement. No nationality is being targeted. The rule of law, individual rights, and due process remain paramount at all times,” it added.

Bacolod seals partnership for MassKara Festival 2026. BACOLOD CITY – Mayor Greg Gasataya and the Bacolod Gugma Foundation, Inc. sealed a partnership for the 2026 MassKara Festival through a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) signed Wednesday, Aug. 19, at the Bacolod City Government Center (BCGC), more than a month ahead of the event. During the signing, Gasataya and Festival Director Rodney Ascalon announced several changes aimed at improving public safety, crowd management, and the overall festival experience. This year’s MassKara Festival carries the theme “Share the Smile. Celebrate Gugma,” highlighting the love, joy, unity, and community spirit that have defined the city’s iconic celebration for generations. The theme also encourages a new generation of Bacolodnons to embrace, reinvent, and carry the MassKara tradition forward. Ascalon said the festival will officially launch in the first week of September, with renewed emphasis on local heritage and grassroots participation. The Miss Bacolod MassKara pageant will also take on a new format. Instead of being open to all Bacolodnons, this year’s 15 candidates will exclusively represent their respective barangays. The grand launch will unveil the festival’s competition lineup, featuring 10 Electric MassKara entries, eight Barangay Category entries, and seven School Category entries for the arena and street dancing competitions. Several venues and arrangements will likewise change. The arena competition is expected to move from the Paglaum Sports Complex to a new venue following safety assessments, while the street dancing competition will take a new route. The grand awarding ceremony, however, will remain at the public plaza. MassKara 2026 will be staged in two phases. Food kiosks will open beginning October 1, with the Pre-MassKara Celebration running from October 1 to 8. This period will feature sports tournaments, pre-pageant activities, mall events, and other community programs. The festival’s major highlights will take place from October 16 to 18. Ascalon, who recently assumed the role of festival director, said he is committed to making MassKara a true celebration of gugma -- the love, unity, and shared spirit of Bacolodnons. He emphasized that MassKara is more than a festival, describing it as a platform that brings people together, creates meaningful experiences, and showcases Bacolod’s warmth, resilience, culture, and creativity to the world. Organizers said the 2026 celebration will continue creating opportunities for every Bacolodnon to participate, contribute, and feel part of the city’s beloved “City of Smiles” tradition.

Olympian Kiyomi Watanabe banners PH judokas in Asian Games. Two-time Olympian Kiyomi Watanabe flies the flag once more as she headlines the Philippine national judo team in the coming 20th Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan next month. The 29-year-old Watanabe spearheads the 8-strong squad together with several multi-medalists in the Southeast Asian Games, including Chino Sy Tancontian, who is also competing in wrestling and sambo events. Eager to bounce back from her seventh-place finish in the women’s -63kg event of the previous edition held in Hangzhou, China nearly three years ago, Watanabe moves to the heavier class in -78kg where she looks to secure a medal this time. She is joined by Sy’s fellow University of Santo Tomas standout Khrizzie Pabulayan. Watanabe’s silver in the Jakarta meet in 2018 is the first and only Asian Games medal of the Philippines in judo so far. Tancontian, on the other hand, sprints into his maiden Asiad action with an aim of a podium finish in the men’s -100kg category. Completing the cast are Daryl John Mercado (-60kg), Keisei Nakano (-66kg), who also competed in 2018 Asiad, Gabriel Benedict Quitain (-73kg), and Eskelen Kedo (+100kg). In the distaff side, rising star Joemari Heart Rafael, who bagged silver in 2025 SEA Games, vies in the women’s -57kg. Apart from Watanabe and Nakano, all remaining members are making their debuts in the continental showpiece.

Erwin Tulfo: Consumers shouldn’t pay for power firms’ failure to modernize. Sen. Erwin Tulfo on Thursday, Aug. 20, questioned whether power companies had sufficiently invested in modernizing their facilities, arguing that consumers should not bear the cost of system losses resulting from outdated infrastructure. During a Senate Committee on Energy hearing, Tulfo said distribution utilities and other power companies may have relied too heavily on system loss charges instead of investing in upgrades to their networks. “I don't know if you'll agree with me. Hindi sila nag-invest through the years yung capital expenditure expenses para to modernize,” Tulfo said. “Because umasa lang po sila diyan sa systems loss na yan. Bakit ako magbabago ng linya? Sisingilin ko lang naman ito si Juan si Maria,” he added. Tulfo made the remarks after Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) Chairperson Atty. Francis Juan explained that distribution utilities are required to meet technical and performance standards and may be penalized for exceeding allowable system loss levels. Juan said utilities also have an incentive to invest in capital expenditure programs to reduce system losses, particularly when their losses exceed the regulatory cap. Tulfo, however, said consumers should not be blamed for utilities' failure to modernize their systems. “It is not our fault, it is not the fault of the consumers na hindi sila nakapag-invest (It is not our fault; it is not the consumers’ fault that they failed to invest),” he said. He said businesses should set aside funds for expansion and modernization rather than rely on consumers to absorb losses. Tulfo also pointed to aging transmission lines and other facilities as possible contributors to system losses, likening outdated power infrastructure to a deteriorating highway that can hamper the movement of electricity. The senator has been pushing for a review of the system loss charges imposed on consumers, particularly the recovery of non-technical losses such as electricity theft, illegal connections, and meter tampering. During the hearing, Juan said the ERC could allow the recovery of system loss costs to be reduced or even set to zero, but warned that abruptly shifting the costs to distribution utilities could put some financially vulnerable electric cooperatives at risk. Juan said a phased implementation may instead be considered to give utilities time to adjust if system loss recovery is eventually prohibited. Tulfo maintained that the burden should not simply be passed on to consumers and questioned whether power companies would actually face bankruptcy if system loss charges were removed. Removing system loss charges Tulfo pressed the ERC on whether electricity distributors, transmission firms, and generation companies could absorb system loss costs if consumers were no longer charged for them. Juan said the government could prohibit or reduce the recovery of both technical and non-technical system losses, but warned that the impact on utilities would have to be considered. Juan said technical losses from the transmission and distribution of electricity could not be completely eliminated, while non-technical losses, including electricity theft and billing errors, could be minimized. He said the government could instead require distribution utilities to shoulder the costs, but suggested that any policy change could be implemented gradually to give utilities time to adjust. Tulfo, however, questioned claims that utilities would suffer severe financial losses if system loss charges were removed, asking whether major players such as Meralco and the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines, as well as electric cooperatives, would actually face bankruptcy or closure. Juan said distribution utilities have varying levels of system losses and financial performance. While some are operating within or below the limits set by the ERC, others—particularly electric cooperatives with high system losses—already absorb part of the costs and could face greater financial difficulties if they are required to shoulder more.

Batching plant supervisor gunned down in Batangas. LIPA CITY, Batangas — A 49‑year‑old batching plant supervisor was shot to death while drinking in front of his house Wednesday night, Aug. 19, in Purok 5, Barangay Rizal. Police identified the victim as Elmer, an employee of Remix Batching Plant and a resident of the area. He sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was declared dead on arrival at Divine Love Medical Center. According to his son Emerson, Elmer was drinking with Van Allen Paul Garcia when four successive gunshots rang out. Emerson rushed outside and saw his father lying on the ground while the gunman, wearing a hat, reloaded his firearm and fired twice more. The suspect fled on a black motorcycle toward Barangay Calamias. Police are investigating the killing.

Philippines signs air deal with Iceland for daily flights. The Philippines has signed an agreement with Iceland to open up traffic rights for daily flights between Manila and Reykjavík, paving the way for a more convenient travel option for Filipinos headed to the majestic land of fire and ice. The Department of Transportation (DOTr) said an initial air services agreement was signed during air negotiation talks in Reykjavík from Aug. 18 to 19. The deal, entered into by the foreign affairs departments of both countries, aims to allow seven flights per week, or one per day, for passenger and cargo services between Manila and Reykjavík. These traffic rights are expected to give airlines from either country greater flexibility to establish services between the capitals, subject to market demand and commercial viability. The prospective service may take the form of direct flights or connecting flights requiring one or more layovers. Acting Transportation Secretary Giovanni Lopez said the initial agreement will serve as the foundation for future aviation relations between the two countries. “[This] will provide our airlines with a framework to explore new opportunities for connectivity between our two countries and, ultimately, between our respective regions,” he said. Lopez expressed optimism that developing air services will bring the two nations closer together despite the massive geographical distance between them. Located in the North Atlantic Ocean, the Nordic island nation of Iceland is a dream tourist destination for many Filipinos due to its mesmerizing landscapes of glaciers, waterfalls, and volcanoes, as well as its front-row access to the northern lights. Iceland is also home to a growing Filipino population, which forms the largest Asian diaspora in the country. Icelandic government data shows that over 3,000 Filipinos were living there as of Jan. 1 this year. Trade cooperation between the two nations is currently facilitated through the Philippines’ free trade agreement with the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), of which Iceland is a member. The DOTr said it will continue coordinating with its Icelandic counterpart and other aviation stakeholders to implement the agreement effectively. It added that it will pursue additional aviation markets, particularly in the Nordic region, to benefit passengers, tourism, and the broader economy. The DOTr also recently signed an agreement with Türkiye to double flights between Manila and Istanbul to 14 per week.

Japan’s Defense Ministry to seek record ¥8.9 trillion in FY '27 budget. TOKYO, Aug. 20 (Jiji Press) -- Japan's Defense Ministry plans to seek a record 8.9 trillion yen in its budget request for fiscal 2027, up from 8,845.4 billion yen for the current fiscal year. The amount of spending, however, is likely to swell further in a draft government budget to be adopted at year-end, because the budget request will include many measures whose costs are not specified ahead of a planned revision of the country's three key security-related documents this year. The budget request, due by the end of this month, will be based on the three pillars of preparing for new ways of warfare utilizing artificial intelligence and other technologies, ensuring sustained operational capabilities in a prolonged conflict and strengthening defense industrial bases, according to government and ruling camp sources. In addition to costs to produce unmanned attack drones capable of long-distance flights, expenses to develop underwater long-range missiles will be included in the budget request as part of efforts to enhance the country's counterattack capabilities to strike enemy bases. The ministry is also expected to seek spending for the establishment of a new agency to support retired Self-Defense Forces members and their families, along with the addition of three bureaus, including one responsible for international policy. In 2022, then Prime Minister Fumio Kishida's administration set the total defense spending for the five years through fiscal 2027 at about 43 trillion yen. Under the administration of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, the fiscal 2025 defense spending reached about 11 trillion yen, including related expenses, achieving the government's target of raising its defense expenditures to 2 pct of Japan's gross domestic product two years ahead of schedule. However, U.S. President Donald Trump's administration has urged Japan to raise its defense spending to at least 3.5 pct of GDP. In this situation, the focus will be the new defense spending target the Takaichi government is expected to set in the upcoming revision of the three documents--the National Security Strategy, the National Defense Strategy and the Defense Buildup Program.

Film director arrested in Laguna on child abuse charges. STA. ROSA CITY, Laguna — Police arrested a 42‑year‑old film director in Barangay Tagapo for alleged violation of the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act. Police identified the suspect as “Direk Erol” of Quezon City. He was nabbed on Aug. 15 at 8:55 a.m. inside a popular mall by operatives of the Laguna Special Operations Unit, the provincial intelligence team, and Sta. Rosa City police. The arrest stemmed from a warrant issued on July 8, 2025, by Judge Fernando Tolosa Sagun of Regional Trial Court Branch 58, Quezon City, for two counts of violating Section 5(b) of Republic Act 7610. Each case carried a recommended bail of P180,000. The suspect is now detained at the Sta. Rosa City Police custodial facility.

Cotabato Province drops beauty pageant, street dancing from Kalivungan Festival amid austerity measures. DAVAO CITY – The provincial government of Cotabato has opted to exclude the beauty pageant contests and the street dancing competition in this year’s iteration of Kalivungan Festival as part of its continuing austerity and fiscal responsibility measures. Gov. Emmylou Taliño-Mendoza said the decision to streamline the festivities allows the provincial government to allocate resources for programs and interventions that directly respond to the needs of its constituents. “This includes our preparations for the anticipated El Niño period from October to February, particularly the planned procurement of rice as part of the Province’s food security and disaster mitigation measures,” Mendoza emphasized in a statement. It can be recalled that the provincial government has recently strengthened its preparation for the possible impact of the El Niño phenomenon. The provincial government has recently released a report from the risk mapping of Project SARAI (Smarter Approaches to Reinvigorate Agriculture as an Industry in the Philippines) of the Department of Science and Technology, stating that the province will experience a mild drought this August. This has prompted Mendoza to impose measures to save water and explore other possible water sources to prepare for the adverse impact of the dry spell. Even with the exclusion of these major events, the governor assured that the annual Kalivungan Festival this year will remain meaningful, vibrant, and focused on activities that celebrate its people, culture, economy, and identity as Cotabateños. Kalivungan Festival is an annual week-long celebration, which culminates in the founding anniversary of the province of Cotabato on September 1. According to local history, the word Kalivungan comes from the local tribe of Erumanen Ne Menuvu term, which means a "gathering of people.” One of the retained traditional activities is the Kavurunun Festival as it highlights the diverse culture, rituals, and practices of different indigenous peoples’ tribes and their role in shaping the history of Cotabato Province. Kavurunan Festival features several cultural presentations such as traditional ritual performances, ethnic instrument playing, indigenous games and tribal dances. The activity brings together members and leaders from indigenous groups like the Erumanen Ne Menuvu, Manobo, Tagabawa, Blaan, Obo Manobo, Teduray, and Ilianen. Moreover, other activities of the Kalivungan Festival are Yaman ng Cotabato Travel and Trade Expo, Kapagana Festival, Museyo Kutawato Fest, sports events, job fair, awards day, drum and lyre competition, and Kumbira sa Kapitolyo.

Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Russia Ukraine In this episode of War & Peace , Olga is joined by Sabine Fischer, senior fellow at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), to discuss her book “The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response”. They unpack how chauvinist politics – defined as a combination of imperialism, sexism and autocracy – have shaped Russian society and politics under President Vladimir Putin and helped pave the way for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. They examine how the war has accelerated chauvinism in Russia, including through pressure on women to have children, rising domestic violence and the repression of feminist and LGBTQI+ activism, while also raising the war’s complex effects on gender relations in Ukraine. They also consider how different outcomes to the war could shape Russia’s future and politics across Europe, what guardrails liberal democracies, including those in the process of re-arming, have against chauvinist shifts, and whether and how chauvinist politics might be reversed. ORIGI, MESSIAS, ADLI E 25 MILIONI PER MILINKOVIC-SAVIC. LOTITO NE CHIEDE 35!!!. Il Milan, dopo lo scioccante siluramento di Paolo Maldini, punta al grande colpo per il calciomercato estivo: Sergej Milinkovic-Savic della Lazio . Lo ha riferito ' SportMediaset '. Il Diavolo, dunque, ha intenzione di andare all'assalto del centrocampista serbo, classe 1995 , che gioca nella Capitale dal 2015 e che ora sembra arrivato al momento dei saluti. Nonostante il contratto di Milinkovic-Savic scadrà tra un anno, il 30 giugno 2024 , il Presidente della Lazio, Claudio Lotito , continua a valutarlo molto. Si parla di 35-40 milioni di euro, per un giocatore che, in fin dei conti, in questa stagione con le Aquile di Maurizio Sarri si è riconfermato come uno dei centrocampisti più forti e completi del panorama calcistico mondiale. Motivo per cui il Milan, pur di metterlo a disposizione di Stefano Pioli in questo calciomercato estivo, sarebbe pronto ad offrire alla Lazio 25 milioni più ben tre contropartite tecniche individuati in Junior Messias , Divock Origi e Yacine Adli. Le contropartite tecniche sarebbero di gradimento per Mister Sarri e si adatterebbero facilmente al suo gioco spettacolare: Adli può ricoprire diversi ruoli del centrocampo e sarebbe un sostituto ideale del capitano biancoazzurro; Messias , visto il flop di Romero e l'età avanzata di Pedro, sarebbe un'ottima alternativa di fascia visto i tanti impegni che aspettano la Lazio; Origi sarebbe una discreta opzione a Ciro Immobile, lasciando crescere con tranquillità il talentuoso Cancellieri. La palla passa a Lotito che attende un rialzo di offerta magari intorno ai 30 milioni e l'inserimento di tre contropartite tecniche di buon livello per concludere l'affare.

CONFERENCE LEAGUE :POSSIBILE 0-3 A TAVOLINO PER LA FIORENTINA. I TIFOSI VIOLA CI SPERANO!!!. Gli otto punti rimediati da Cristiano Biraghi in finale di Conference League contro il West Ham hanno fatto molto discutere, non soltanto per il gesto vergognoso. Tra le questioni affrontate anche quella dell’interruzione della partita e del 3-0 a tavolino, provvedimenti su cui l’arbitro Del Cerro Grande, da norma, non può nulla. È la Commissione Disciplinare Uefa a decidere. Andiamo quindi a spulciare il regolamento. Tra i casi in cui i club devono rispondere delle azioni della tifoseria c’è anche “il lancio di oggetti che possa mettere in pericolo l’integrità fisica di altri presenti alla partita o pregiudicarne lo svolgimento”. Il paradosso è che Biraghi, per sperare in un 3-0 a tavolino, avrebbe dovuto accentuare il dolore e farsi sostituire, invece è stato “colpevole” di essersi grintosamente rialzato. Per dare un’idea del modo in cui viene messo in pratica il regolamento, prendiamo in esame un caso simile: il famoso petardo in testa a Dida nel derby di Milano del 2004-2005. In quel caso le autorità capiscono che la situazione non può avere seguito e inoltre il brasiliano resta a terra. Per questo motivo, viene assegnato il 3-0 a tavolino ai rossoneri.
